subject: Dedicated capacity: Cerebrum pilot - throughput/SLO mapping and commit tradeoffs
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cerebrumhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing question — tokens/sec / SLA mapping

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re lining up a timeboxed pilot for our clinical summarization feature and need a quick capacity estimate to feed procurement. High level:
- Estimated production traffic (pilot): 600k tokens/day average, with peak bursts of ~120 tokens/sec sustained for ~10–20 minutes during daytime testing windows.
- Target SLO: p95 response latency < 300ms for single-turn generation (no tool calls).
- Model we plan to use for evaluation: community-13B (quantized) with typical prompt length ~60 tokens and response ~120 tokens.

Three asks:
1) Rough tokens/sec -> GPU count mapping and recommended safety headroom for a 3-month pilot.
2) Best-guess on p95 latency map to common SKUs (A100/80GB vs A10 vs T4).
3) Any minimum commitment you’d recommend to balance cost vs reliability (we want low risk of throttling during daytime tests).

If helpful I can share our expected daily traffic by hour. We need something we can hand to procurement Monday.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Senior PM, AI Integrations
Cerebrum Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — tokens/sec / SLA mapping

Daniel — thanks for the clear breakdown. Attached is a quick model (Cerebrum_Throughput_Model.xlsx) with our back-of-envelope numbers and the assumptions. Short answers up front, then details:

Summary recommendations:
- Base recommendation: reserve a committed slab equivalent to 8x A100-40GB GPUs for the pilot, plus a 4x A10 burst pool for daytime tests.
- Why: community-13B (int8-ish) gives roughly 220–320 tokens/sec per A100 depending on prompt/response mix; A10s are ~90–140 tok/s.
- SLO fit: with an A100 serving path and continuous batching disabled for single-turn latency, p95 ≈ 220–280ms (matches your <300ms target) with ~20% headroom if you commit 8x A100 for steady-state plus burst.

Key notes from the spreadsheet (high-level):
- Assumptions: model = community-13B quantized; avg generation tokens = 120; concurrency target at 120 tok/s peak -> approx 1.1 concurrent in-flight generations if one request is 120 tokens over 1–1.2s. We convert peak tokens/sec into effective inference tokens/sec by factoring model throughput and average response length.
- Mapping example: 1 x A100 (40GB, optimized kernel set) ≈ 280 tok/s (batch=1 latency p95 ≈ 250ms).
  - So peak 120 tok/s could be served by a single A100 nominally, but that leaves zero headroom and no room for spikes or retries.
- We recommend 2x nominal capacity for safety (so plan for 560 tok/s equivalent) which maps to ~2 A100s for throughput but because of availability, redundancy, and autoscaling granularity we recommend a committed pool size = 8 A100s (explained below) for operational predictability and to meet your daytime concurrency patterns and future burst comfort.

Operational rationale for larger slab:
- Customer-facing pilots often see correlated bursts and retry storms; reserved capacity avoids noisy neighbor effects and reduces cold-start risk.
- Our Dedicated product allows you to pin CPUs/GPU slabs and set autoscale burst budgets; committing 8x allows predictable p95 tail under canary load and gives ops room for background tasks (model warm-up, cache priming) without impacting the production lane.

I attached the XLS with the token/sec mapping and cost delta scenarios (1x/2x/4x headroom). Let me know if you want us to tailor the sheet to your hourly profile.

Next steps in parallel: we can pull an ops playbook for fallbacks (lower-capacity model variant, quantized vs float, or regional routing). If you want a formal commit quote I’ll loop Ben to draft pricing and the mutual action plan.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — Pilot runbook + headroom math

Laura / team — quick technical notes to add to the customer-facing spreadsheet:

1) Detailed tokens/sec assumptions (per our perf bench):
   - community-13B (int8 optimized kernel)
     - A100-40GB: 260–300 tok/s (p95 latency window 220–280ms)
     - A10: 100–130 tok/s (p95 420–600ms)
     - T4: 50–80 tok/s (p95 often >700ms for p95)

2) Concurrency conversion: use average response length (120 tokens) and peak tokens/sec -> compute concurrent in-flight requests = peak_tok_s * avg_resp_tokens / model_throughput_per_gpu. Example: 120 * 120 / 280 ≈ 51 in-flight token-steps which maps to ~0.43 concurrent CPU-bound requests (model pipeline overlaps reduce to sub-1 numbers). This is why token/sec can be a better sizing metric than raw QPS.

3) Headroom policy options (choose one):
   - Conservative (recommended for pilot with clinical SLAs): 2x peak tokens/sec committed + 30% burst pool.
   - Cost-focused: 1.25x peak tokens/sec committed + autoscale to cover additional bursts (risk: provisioning lag).

4) Proposed concrete plan for Cerebrum pilot:
   - Committed slab: 8x A100-40GB (maps to ~2.2k–2.4k tok/s nominal).
   - Burst pool: 4x A10s (on-demand) to soak short daytime spikes.
   - Fallbacks: smaller quantized variant + lateral routing to lower-cost region if latency allows.

5) SLO guardrails to include in contract: p95 < 300ms when routed to committed slab; automatic fallback to burst pool for transient capacity and a max throttling window of 30s before retry policy.

I also added a small sensitivity table in the sheet showing how p95 shifts with 10% increases in prompt/response size.

-Jonas
